summary: Motygino Airport (MJY) is a small regional airfield serving the remote village of Motygino in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Siberia, Russia. Located near the Yenisei River in one of the most sparsely populated regions of Russia, it primarily supports local air connectivity, including occasional general aviation, charter, and essential transport services for the surrounding taiga communities. The airport plays a vital role in linking this isolated part of Eastern Siberia to larger regional hubs, especially during the harsh winter months when road travel becomes difficult.
faqs:
Q: What type of airport is Motygino Airport?
A: It is a small regional airport serving the village of Motygino in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Siberia, primarily handling general aviation and limited scheduled services.

Q: Does Motygino Airport offer international flights?
A: No, Motygino Airport is a domestic-only facility serving local and regional routes within Russia.

Q: How can I reach Motygino from the airport?
A: The airport is located close to the village center, and onward travel is typically by local road transport, private vehicle, or pre-arranged pickup.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Motygino?
A: Air services are generally more reliable in winter and shoulder seasons when roads through the surrounding taiga become difficult to traverse.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a short distance from the village of Motygino, so ground transportation is limited; arranging a local pickup in advance is strongly recommended. During winter months, frozen roads and river ice roads may serve as alternative routes, but air access remains the most reliable year-round option. There is no scheduled public transit directly serving the airport, so travelers should coordinate ground transport before arrival.
local_tip: Bring layered clothing and be prepared for significant temperature swings — Motygino sits deep in the Siberian taiga, where winter temperatures can plunge well below -30°C, even mild days can feel cold due to wind off the Yenisei River.
